name: io.github.Nero-Engine/site-pack
title: Site Pack
description: Live Article 4, listed building, flood zone and waste carrier checks, plus permitted development

tools.name: list_capabilities
tools.description: Lists Site Pack's tools, the date its rules were last checked, what it covers (nations, project types, work types) and what it deliberately does not do. Free, needs no input.

tools.name: check_permitted_development
tools.description: Checks a householder project in England against the permitted development limits in the GPDO 2015, Schedule 2, Part 1: single and multi storey rear extensions, side and wraparound extensions (Class A), loft dormers and hip to gable (Class B), rooflights (Class C), porches (Class D), outbuildings and garden rooms (Class E), and adding storeys (Class AA). Returns `verdict` (permitted_development, prior_approval_route, needs_planning_permission, needs_listed_building_consent, check_article_4_or_condition, needs_more_info, not_covered), `answer`, one line per limit in `checks` (status pass, fail or needs_input, with the limit and the rule's paragraph), the larger home extension prior approval route when a single storey rear extension is 3 to 6 m (attached) or 4 to 8 m (detached), flags for conservation areas, National Parks, National Landscapes, listed buildings and Article 4, `must_confirm` and sources. Example: 3.5 m single storey rear extension on a semi, 3.8 m high: {"project":"rear_extension_single_storey","house_type":"semi_detached","depth_m":3.5,"height_m":3.8,"eaves_height_m":2.8,"within_2m_of_boundary":true,"curtilage_coverage_percent":20,"materials_similar":true,"higher_than_existing_roof":false,"eaves_higher_than_existing":false,"beyond_principal_or_highway_side_elevation":false,"balcony_veranda_or_raised_platform":false}.

nation.description: Defaults to england. Only england is checked; others return not_covered.

property_kind.description: Defaults to house. Flats and maisonettes have no householder permitted development.

house_type.description: Needed for rear extensions (4 m detached, 3 m otherwise) and lofts (40 m3 terraced or end terrace, 50 m3 otherwise).

designations.description: Any that apply at the address. national_landscape is the new name for an AONB. Leave empty if none.

depth_m.description: Rear extensions: how far it projects beyond the rear wall of the ORIGINAL house, metres.

height_m.description: Highest point of the extension, porch or outbuilding above ground, metres.

storeys.description: Storeys in the extension or outbuilding.

distance_to_rear_boundary_m.description: Multi storey rear extensions: distance from the extension to the boundary opposite the rear wall.

width_m.description: Side extensions: width of the extension.

original_house_width_m.description: Side extensions: width of the original house.

curtilage_coverage_percent.description: After the work: ground covered by all buildings other than the original house, as a % of the plot excluding the original house footprint.

beyond_principal_or_highway_side_elevati.description: Does it go forward of the front (principal) wall, or of a side wall facing a road?

balcony_veranda_or_raised_platform.description: Includes a balcony, veranda, or a raised platform (decking) over 0.3 m high.

materials_similar.description: External materials look similar to the house.

side_windows_obscure_and_fixed.description: Upper floor or roof windows in a side wall are obscure glazed and non-opening below 1.7 m.

roof_pitch_matches.description: Multi storey: roof pitch matches the house as far as practical.

cladding.description: Article 2(3) land: will the outside be clad in stone, render, pebble dash, timber, plastic or tiles?

added_volume_m3.description: Lofts: extra roof space volume including any earlier roof enlargements, m3.

on_front_slope_facing_highway.description: Lofts: does the dormer go on the front roof slope facing a road?

hip_to_gable.description: Lofts: is it a hip to gable (no eaves set back needed)?

eaves_setback_m.description: Lofts: dormer set back from the eaves along the slope, metres (at least 0.2).

protrusion_m.description: Rooflights: how far it stands proud of the roof slope, metres.

floor_area_m2.description: Porches: external ground floor area. Outbuildings: footprint.

distance_to_highway_boundary_m.description: Porches: distance to the boundary with a road or footway.

forward_of_principal_elevation.description: Outbuildings: in front of the house's front wall?

roof_type.description: Outbuildings: dual pitched allows 4 m (if not within 2 m of a boundary).

distance_from_house_m.description: Outbuildings in National Parks, National Landscapes, the Broads or World Heritage Sites.

tools.name: check_building_regs
tools.description: For one or more kinds of building work in England or Wales: is it notifiable building work, exempt (small outbuildings, ground level conservatories and porches up to 30 m2), self-certifiable by a competent person scheme (FENSA, Certass, HETAS, OFTEC, CompetentRoofer), or must it go to the Building Safety Regulator (higher-risk buildings, England). Says whether a building notice is allowed or full plans are required (non-domestic, common parts of flats, within 3 m of a public sewer), and lists the Parts of Schedule 1 likely to apply with the reason for each (indicative). Returns `verdict`, `notifiable`, per-work reasons, routes, `parts_likely_to_apply`, `must_confirm` and sources. Example: {"work":["single_storey_extension","remove_load_bearing_wall"],"within_3m_of_public_sewer":false}.

nation.description: Defaults to england. Scotland and Northern Ireland return not_covered.

work.description: All the kinds of work in the job.

floor_area_m2.description: Outbuildings, conservatories and porches: internal floor area.

sleeping_accommodation.description: Outbuildings: will anyone sleep in it?

mainly_non_combustible.description: Outbuildings of 15 to 30 m2: built mainly of non-combustible materials?

separated_by_external_doors.description: Conservatories and porches: separated from the house by external quality walls, doors or windows?

heated_from_house_system.description: Conservatories: heated by extending the house heating?

area_renovated_percent.description: Re-roofing, re-rendering, wall insulation: share of that roof or wall area being renovated, %.

higher_risk_building.description: England: at least 18 m or 7 storeys with at least 2 homes (or a care home or hospital of that height).

competent_person_scheme.description: If the installer is a member of one (for windows, stoves, roofs).

tools.name: party_wall_notices
tools.description: Works out which notice the Party Wall etc. Act 1996 needs (line of junction, section 1; party structure, sections 2 and 3; adjacent excavation within 3 m or 6 m, section 6), and the dates: from `planned_start_date` the latest day to send it by the chosen method (by hand, first or second class post, email if agreed), or from `serve_date` the day it counts as served and the earliest start; plus the neighbour's 14 day reply deadline, when a dispute is deemed to arise, and when the notice lapses (12 months). Uses England and Wales bank holidays to 2028. Returns `notice`, `section`, `dates` (each as YYYY-MM-DD plus plain words), step by step `working`, what the notice must say, warnings and sources. Example: cutting a steel beam into a party wall, work to start 1 March 2027, posted first class: {"work":"insert_beam_or_dpc_into_party_wall","planned_start_date":"2027-03-01","serve_method":"first_class_post"}.

nation.description: Defaults to england. The Act applies in England and Wales only.

planned_start_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Give this or serve_date (or both, to check the start is late enough).

serve_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD: the day the notice was or will be handed over, posted or emailed.

adjoining_owners.description: How many adjoining owners (each gets their own notice). Defaults to 1.

excavation_depth_m.description: Excavations: depth of your excavation or foundation below ground.

distance_to_neighbour_building_m.description: Excavations: horizontal distance from the excavation to the neighbour's building.

neighbour_foundation_depth_m.description: Excavations: depth of the neighbour's foundations, if known.

tools.name: cdm_duties
tools.description: For a construction project in Great Britain (domestic by default): who holds the client's duties (on a domestic job they pass to the contractor, the principal contractor, or the principal designer under a written agreement), which roles must be filled (principal designer and principal contractor when there is more than one contractor), the core duties (construction phase plan, welfare, induction, health and safety file), and whether the project must be notified to HSE on form F10 (longer than 30 working days with more than 20 workers at once, or over 500 person days), with the arithmetic shown. Returns `f10_notification_needed`, `f10_answer`, `client_duties_held_by`, `roles`, `duties`, `working`, `must_confirm` and sources. Example: an extension with 4 trades, 60 working days, peak 6 on site, average 3: {"contractors":4,"duration_working_days":60,"peak_workers_on_site":6,"average_workers_on_site":3}.

client_type.description: Defaults to domestic (a homeowner having work done on their own home, not as a business).

contractors.description: Firms and self-employed trades working on the project, including subcontractors. 1 if only you.

duration_working_days.description: Expected length of the construction work in working days.

peak_workers_on_site.description: Most people working on site at the same time.

average_workers_on_site.description: Typical number on site, used to estimate person days.

person_days.description: Total person days, if already known.

designer_agreed_to_take_client_duties.description: Domestic only: has the client a written agreement for the principal designer to take on the client duties?

tools.name: estimate_materials
tools.description: Works out quantities from dimensions, with the working: bricks (60 a m2 per half brick leaf), blocks (about 10 a m2), cavity walls with ties, mortar from wall volume minus unit volume, cement bags and sand tonnes for a chosen mix, concrete for strip foundations and slabs (ready mix order rounded up to 0.25 m3, or site mixed 1:2:4 materials), and plasterboard sheets by size. Openings are deducted. Waste allowances default to bricks and blocks 5%, mortar 10%, concrete 5%, plasterboard 10% and can be changed. Returns `order` (what to buy), per item `working`, totals before waste and notes. Example: a 6 m by 2.4 m cavity wall with a 1.2 m2 window, plus a 6 m strip foundation 0.6 m wide and 1 m deep: {"items":[{"kind":"cavity_wall","length_m":6,"height_m":2.4,"openings_m2":1.2},{"kind":"strip_foundation","length_m":6,"width_m":0.6,"depth_m":1}]}.

openings_m2.description: Walls: total area of windows and doors to deduct.

block_thickness_mm.description: Block and cavity walls. Defaults to 100.

waste_percent.description: Override any of: bricks, blocks, mortar, concrete, plasterboard (percent).

mortar_mix_sand_parts.description: Sand parts to 1 cement, defaults to 5 (1:5). Use what the specification says.

tools.name: structural_triage
tools.description: First-response triage when a customer reports a crack, a bulging or leaning wall, a sagging or fallen ceiling, a collapse, storm damage to a roof or chimney, a fallen tree or vehicle impact, a sagging floor, problems after a wall was removed, or signs of subsidence. Cautious by design: any danger to people makes it an emergency. Returns `urgency` (emergency, soon or routine: the same three speeds Nero Work uses), reasons, `safe_first_steps`, who to call now (999, gas 0800 111 999, power 105, the council dangerous structures team, insurer, structural engineer), and the questions to ask if details are missing. Example: a ceiling bulging with water under a bathroom: {"problem":"ceiling_sagging_or_fallen","water_coming_in":true}.

near_road_or_footway.description: Could it fall onto a road, footway or neighbour's property?

new_cracks_or_sagging_above.description: After a wall was removed or an impact: new cracks or sagging above?

tools.name: site_constraints
tools.description: Looks up, live from official open data, what applies at the customer's postcode before an extension, loft, porch, outbuilding or groundworks: Article 4 directions (permitted development removed), listed buildings, conservation areas, World Heritage Sites, National Landscapes, scheduled monuments, flood risk zones and Tree Preservation Orders (planning.data.gov.uk, England, councils that publish). Returns each constraint found with its source link, what it means for the build, and the `designations` to pass straight to check_permitted_development. A constraint not found is not proof of none: the answer says so. Example: {"postcode":"YO1 7HH"}.

tools.name: waste_carrier_check
tools.description: Searches the Environment Agency public register of waste carriers, brokers and dealers (England) live, by registration number (for example CBDU123456) or business name with an optional postcode. Returns each match with its tier (upper tier may carry other people's waste, lower tier only its own), registration and expiry dates, status, address and a link to the register entry, plus links to the Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland registers. Use it for the builder's own registration or a skip, grab or muck away firm. Example: {"name":"Oakline Building","postcode":"LS6 2AB"}.

postcode.description: Narrows a name search to that postcode or area.

tools.name: trade_profile
tools.description: Checks the builder's own business details (Nero Trade Profile v1: trading name, Companies House number, trade body or scheme and membership number such as FMB or TrustMark, postcode, contact) and returns them cleaned, with a stable `nero_trade_ref` computed from the scheme membership or company number. The same object, given as `trade` to the other tools, prefills their answers. Site Pack stores nothing. The same profile and reference can later be used to sign the business into Nero Work, the agent job exchange for trades.
